meta.title: U.S. reality layer
meta.scope: Public, aggregate, United States national baseline
meta.warning: Authorized end strength is not the same as deployed strength, readiness, availability, or local response capacity.

realityChecks.title: End strength is a ceiling or authorization
realityChecks.text: It is a personnel-strength figure for a fiscal year, not a count of units ready to deploy immediately or a prediction of what can be committed to a particular crisis.

realityChecks.title: Readiness is distributed unevenly
realityChecks.text: Training cycles, maintenance, personnel availability, prepositioning, geography, and mission assignments matter more than a national personnel total for a specific event.

realityChecks.title: Domestic response has legal and political constraints
realityChecks.text: Federal, state, territorial, and local authorities have different roles. Reserve and National Guard availability can change with mobilization, existing missions, and state authority.

realityChecks.title: Civilian effects are infrastructure-mediated
realityChecks.text: For households, the practical pathway is usually through power, water, fuel, communications, health care, payments, transportation, and supply chains—not a simple battlefield front line.
